result:
I checked all 24 claims on the 16 held pages against their images: 23 confirmed, 1 judged real but not serious. The verdicts are in `/data/scratch/sl/jobs/zh-held-quality-8053/second/out/held.json`.

- **Margin title read as commentary (most of the claims).** On many Siku Quanshu pages, the margin title 欽定四庫全書 is misread as a quoted line such as "次定曰…". The English then turns that line into an invented commentator "Ci Ding", an invented lacuna ("three and a half sentences missing"), an invented margin note, or invented notes about characters. I confirmed every one of these. I put the transcription-only claims at medium confidence, because a reader of the Chinese might recognise the junk.
- **The one I downgraded.** 前漢書 vol. 52, p. 40 is marked `real_not_serious`. The invented Yan Shigu note there is an empty pronunciation remark and says nothing false about the history.
- **Other confirmed errors:**
  - 前漢書 vol. 52, p. 114: the speaker is reversed, so the Han envoy is given King Hu's words.
  - 前漢書 vol. 2, p. 10: a moon eclipse is invented. The subject is the dragons on the previous page. I'd reclassify this as a page-seam error (T6), not translation over garbled text (T7), because the transcription is correct.
  - 三國志 vol. 3, p. 18: the English adds day-of-month glosses the source doesn't give, and the two contradict each other.
  - 三國志 vol. 6, p. 45: "to declare themselves king" is invented at the page break.
  - 史記 vol. 37, p. 25: the source's "excess" (太過) is translated as "deficiency".
  - 楚辭集註, p. 146: a whole column of main text is missing from the transcription.
  - 金匱要略, p. 169: the dose of 桂枝 (一兩) is dropped.
  - 遠鏡說, p. 3: a line crediting the work to Ricci is invented. I mirrored the show-through to check: it is the back page's 天啓六年 colophon, so the line isn't even a misreading of it.
- **Lowest-confidence call.** 尚書韻 p. 10 depends on one cursive character. Enlarged, it looks like 明 rather than 非, so I confirmed the claim at medium confidence.
